title: Cartier line bundle and canonical section under Cartier preserving pullback
statement: Let $h:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $D\hookrightarrow T$ be an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Assume the scheme-theoretic pullback $D'=T'\times_TD$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is again an effective Cartier divisor. Then there is a canonical isomorphism $h^*\mathcal O_T(D)\cong\mathcal O_{T'}(D')$, where the divisor line bundles and module pullback are [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle, def-pc-module-pullback], carrying the canonical section of $\mathcal O_T(D)$ to the canonical section of $\mathcal O_{T'}(D')$. On the complements, this isomorphism carries the canonical trivialization to the pulled-back trivialization. Here the canonical section of $\mathcal O_T(D)=\mathcal I_D^\vee$ is the dual of the ideal inclusion $\mathcal I_D\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_T$; on $T-D$ it is a basis and defines the stated trivialization, and likewise on $T'-D'$.

proof.text: Construct the map phi from the ordinary pullback of J to J.comap h by the kernel universal property, factoring the pulled ideal inclusion. It satisfies phi followed by the inverse-image ideal inclusion = the pulled inclusion followed by the structure-sheaf identification. Repeat the local-generator argument of the proved source EffectiveCartier.nonempty_pullback_toModules_iso while retaining this equation. Near a point choose J=(b) and lift b to a section s. Trivialize the pulled ideal with basis e and write the pulled s=a e. The inverse-image ideal is generated by g=h-sharp(b); write the image of phi(e) as a-prime g. The inclusion equation gives (a a-prime-1)g=0. The affine-generator regularity of [lem-pc-cartier-affine-generator-regular] gives a a-prime=1, so a-prime is a unit and phi(e) freely generates the inverse-image ideal. The source isIso_of_isFreeGenerator criterion makes phi an isomorphism. The local criterion includes empty schemes and zero section rings.

Transport this isomorphism along the adjunction-normalized comparison from explicit tensor pullback to ordinary pullback. Under the adjunction the composite of this comparison at the structure sheaf with the ordinary unit identification is the structure-sheaf map, so injectivity of the Hom equivalence identifies it with epsilon_h of [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf]. Naturality of the comparison therefore gives an isomorphism a:P_h J -> J-prime with a followed by the ideal inclusion equal to P_h of the original inclusion followed by epsilon_h.

For every map f:M -> N prove P_h(dual f) followed by delta_M equals delta_N followed by dual(P_h f), where delta is the transposed evaluation comparison of [lem-sc-picard-canonical-base-change-comparisons]. Apply injectivity of uncurrying. The naturality of the transported tensor comparison and the precomposition/evaluation identity identify the two resulting maps. The tensor-comparison naturality itself follows by expanding its definition and using naturality of the adjunction comparison and the ordinary pullback monoidal structure.

The ideal module J and the unit module are finite locally free, so [lem-sc-picard-tensor-dual-comparison-iso] makes both delta maps invertible. Define e=delta_J followed by dual(a inverse). Apply the preceding naturality with f the ideal inclusion. In the canonical-section expression the inverse delta_unit cancels delta_unit. Contravariant functoriality of duality reduces the remaining expression to dual(a inverse followed by P_h inclusion followed by epsilon_h). The equation of step 2 and a inverse followed by a = identity make it the dual of the inverse-image ideal inclusion, exactly the required equality. Restricting this equality to the complements preserves the canonical bases and hence their trivializations.
